article.title: How to choose a website traffic monitoring tool: features and tradeoffs to compare

topics.angle: How to choose a website traffic monitoring tool: features and tradeoffs to compare
topics.audience: Small business website owners seeking simpler analytics alternatives

topics.angle: How to track revenue from your website traffic on your own site

findings.text: For the checkout scenario above, Cloudflare Web Analytics is ruled out immediately: it keeps only six months of history and can't track a custom "purchase completed" event, so year-over-year comparison and conversion tracking are both off the table. Cloudflare also aggregates larger historical reports down to roughly 10% of original volume after seven days, meaning older totals become estimates rather than direct counts. Matomo can technically do everything you need, but its depth (dozens of reports, visitor-level data) means more setup and more privacy configuration to strip out cookies before you're consent-banner-free. Plausible fits the brief directly: goals and revenue tracking for checkout events, funnels for the checkout sequence, and data retention starting at 3 years on the Starter plan, without a consent banner. Matomo's own pricing wasn't part of the pages we drew from here, so check that directly against your traffic volume before deciding.
findings.reason: Implies funnels/revenue attribution ship with Starter's 3-year retention, but source ties those features to the Business plan (5-year retention).

findings.text: Broad reporting depth, includes visitor-level views

requirements: What real-time monitoring capabilities does each tool offer, and how frequently do dashboards update?
What is the pricing structure for each tool, and what traffic/pageview limits apply at each tier?
Which visitor behavior tracking features (conversions, goals, funnels, user journeys) does each tool include as standard?
What privacy and data handling practices does each tool employ regarding cookies, data storage, and compliance?
